banners.name: showcase-desk
banners.title: Desk and phones
banners.description: The workbench in a desktop window (Warren truss, member M12 selected, its inspector open; Light) between a Dark phone with the overloaded Pratt and its inspector sheet and a Light phone with the Howe roof truss, on the light blueprint sheet.

banners.name: showcase-phones
banners.title: Three phones
banners.description: Three phones on a deep blueprint ground: the Warren truss with its inspector sheet (Dark), the Howe roof in Utilization (Light, centre, raised) and the overloaded Pratt with its red failure pills (Dark).

banners.name: showcase-daynight
banners.title: Day and night
banners.description: The Warren truss on the light sheet in front, the same truss in Utilization on the dark drafting table behind, on a ground that turns from paper to night.

banners.name: focus-truss
banners.title: The truss canvas
banners.description: The Skia truss canvas at night: the Warren sample's member forces drawn by line style (tension open, compression hatched), loads, reactions, the deflected ghost and the dimension chain, laid back on the drafting table.

banners.name: focus-utilization
banners.title: Utilization ramp
banners.description: The Warren truss in Utilization mode (Dark): members on the ramp from Primary through Warn towards Error with percent labels, and the inspector's result for the 87 % end post M12.

banners.name: focus-failure
banners.title: Failure highlight
banners.description: An overloaded Pratt truss on the light sheet: red BUCKLES pills with utilization, dashed red Euler bows on the failing struts, and the inspector's failure list worst first.

banners.name: focus-palette
banners.title: Command palette
banners.description: The Ctrl+K command palette searched for "toggle" (six view toggles with their shortcuts), sharp over the blurred Dark workbench it opens on.

banners.name: stylized-split
banners.title: Light and Dark split
banners.description: One workbench, Light and Dark, on one turned window cut by a single diagonal at the Warren web's 63.4 degree angle.

banners.name: stylized-stack
banners.title: Tracing layers
banners.description: The Warren sample's canvas in four renderings (Forces and Utilization, Light and Dark) stacked like tracing layers, tied by dashed construction lines.

banners.name: stylized-mosaic
banners.title: Preset wall
banners.description: The six parametric presets (Pratt, Howe, Warren, K truss, Fink and scissor roof) at their defaults, Light and Dark alternating, as a tilted wall of drawing sheets with soft outer columns.

banners.name: focus-truss-titled
banners.title: Truss canvas, titled
banners.description: focus-truss with the display name set as the app's own wordmark: LOADPATH in JetBrains Mono Medium in Dark Primary.

notes: The Release WebAssembly build has the app's own Debug fixtures compiled in (src/tools/sample-hooks.targets) so captures open on the samples and presets by environment variable; every state shown is also reachable through the UI (sample buttons, Presets), nothing was typed or edited.

Captures come from five sessions of the same build (src/tools/sessions/); the app has no clock and its fixtures and solver are deterministic, so figures agree across frames (M12 87 %, 41.93 kN; Pratt 294 %). Only the status bar's solve time differs (0.7 or 1.1 ms).
showcase-desk pairs the desktop session with the phone session, and focus-utilization pairs the canvas session with the inspector session: same build and data, not one browser session.

Turned planes (perspective) are resampled once by Chromium's compositor, so their text is about one device pixel softer than flat captures at 2x; no capture is shown above its native pixels, and the palette, inspector cards and phones are flat.
Showcase banners show whole screens, so their UI text is below 10 px at 1x, as in the house-style banners; the mosaic's and the stack's sheet text is decorative and not meant to be read.
The titled variant uses JetBrains Mono Medium, the app's wordmark face (Inter is the UI text face).
